title: paged-kv-cache: block manager improvements (allocator, reuse, pinning)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache block manager: faster allocation, reduced memory churn, and optional pinning to prevent eviction of hot KV blocks. Improves 95th pct latency and throughput for batched generation workloads.
description:
Context: The paged KV cache block manager is the hot path for long-context batched inference. We observed fragmentation and high allocation overhead under continuous batching, which caused transient latency spikes and increased peak GPU memory. This PR implements a focused set of improvements: 1) a dedicated block allocator with size-classed free lists, 2) block reuse across sessions to reduce churn, and 3) an explicit pinning API for hot KV blocks to avoid eviction during critical requests.

Changes: Implemented a new allocator (allocator.rs) with power-of-two size classes and per-thread freelists; added block_manager.rs refactor to use the allocator and expose pin/unpin semantics; added a lightweight LRU-like reuse policy to prefer recently freed blocks matching size/shape; added accounting and metrics (kv.block_reuse_hits, kv.block_allocations, kv.pinned_blocks); extended continuous batching integration tests to validate reuse and eviction behavior under high multiplexing; added bench for 8/16/32 token sequences to measure throughput/latency.

Rationale: Size-class freelists dramatically reduce the cost of repeated allocations when many small KV pages are created by attention tiling and dynamic kv growth. Pinning provides an escape hatch for routes where evicting warm KV state causes a large recomputation cost. Reuse reduces pressure on GPU allocator and lowers fragmentation that previously triggered expensive device synchronizations.

Compatibility and upgrade notes: On-disk/in-memory page format is unchanged; the allocator is purely in-process and falls back to previous behavior if disabled. Pinning is opt-in via a route-level config (default: off) to avoid surprising memory increases in tight capacity clusters.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for allocator and block manager; integration tests with continuous batching harness; 48-hour stage canary on Dedicated capacity with 10% traffic. Observability dashboards added for reuse rate and pin counts to validate behavior during rollout.

review_comments: Marco Li: Can we avoid global locks here? Suggest per-thread freelists with a fallback to a global pool. - Addressed in allocator.rs with per-thread freelists and CAS-protected global pool.
Sofia Nguyen: Add metrics to understand reuse vs allocation rate during canary. - Added kv.block_reuse_hits, kv.block_allocations and dashboard in docs/ops/paged-kv.md.
Rahul Menon: Pinning is powerful but can cause OOM if used incorrectly; add an opt-in config and guardrails. - Added route-level config and a cluster-level soft limit with eviction warnings.
ci_checks: bench/kv_cache: initial run showed 1.8% regression, fixed allocator hot-path, final run: pass (+18% throughput)
summary_metrics: throughput: +18% on microbench with batch=16, seq=32
peak-gpu-memory: -27% for multiplexed workloads due to reduced fragmentation
testing: Unit tests for allocator and block manager (cross-platform)
Integration tests with continuous batching harness simulated 2k concurrent sessions
48-hour stress canary on Dedicated (10% traffic) monitoring reuse and pin metrics
Manual regression bench against vector of sequence lengths (8/16/32/64)
migration_notes: No data migrations required; page format unchanged
Pinning default is off; operators must enable route.pinned_kv=true to use
If cluster-level soft pin limit is hit, system emits warnings and starts best-effort eviction
future_work: Introduce adaptive size-class tuning based on workload histograms (ENG-4578)

Expose finer-grained eviction policies via route config and SLO-driven heuristics
